paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this one. The Pharisees' disciples and the Herodians came with a question built like a trap, and Jesus saw it coming. He knew their evil intent (Matthew 22:18). Nobody can sweet-talk their way past Him, and that is GOOD news for a baker who's trying to learn from Him.

Now look at what He does with that coin. He asks whose image and inscription are on it, and they answer, "Caesar's." Then He says, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." (Matthew 22:21). I think the lesson is that there are two questions in your wallet. One is what you owe the world around you, and the other is what belongs to God, and Jesus doesn't let the first one swallow the second.

So take the coin home with you, friend. The coin carried Caesar's image, and a whole lot more than a coin carries God's. Genesis 1:27 says God created man in His own image, so I think that question about whose image is on something has a bigger answer than they planned for. Give God what is God's, and keep your oven ready, because this story is not finished yet.
